editorial_rule: Data points where to look; the game proves the story.
voice: Notice it. Name it. Connect it to the stakes. Then play ball.

editorial_frame.angle: Multiple division races have compressed at once; Dallas–Detroit is the lead example, and the other races show that the pressure is league-wide rather than isolated.
editorial_frame.why_lead: Dallas–Detroit is a high-confidence, two-game current race and connects to a separate Detroit attendance fact without requiring invented emotion.
editorial_frame.supporting_picture: San Francisco–Phoenix is also two games, Las Vegas–Seattle is three, and Las Vegas–Denver supplies an unplayed July 20 field-level setup.

lead_story.title: Dallas Rustlers leads Detroit Dukes by 2 game(s) in National Baseball Conference Central Division
lead_story.evidence_summary: Through July 19: Dallas Rustlers 52-41; Detroit Dukes 50-43.
lead_story.why_it_matters: With fewer games remaining, each direct result has less schedule left to absorb it.
lead_story.recommended_use: Baseball Observer main segment|Daily 411|forum written post
lead_story.proven: Dallas is 52-41 and Detroit is 50-43 through games completed July 19; Dallas leads by two games.
lead_story.do_not_overstate: The division is not settled. Do not infer Detroit fan sentiment from attendance or assign managerial blame.
talking_points: Here’s the skinny: two games separate Dallas and Detroit in the NBC Central.
The records establish the pressure—52-41 against 50-43—with less schedule left to absorb each result.
Detroit’s listed attendance leads the league, which gives the race public scale without telling us what those fans feel.
Data points where to look; the next games prove whether the margin changes.
lead_story.transition: Dallas–Detroit is not an isolated squeeze. The NBC West is also separated by two games, so move next to San Francisco–Phoenix.
